newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ford's Brazil unit faces Brazil investigation.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Brazil unit faces Brazil investigation.

text.p: Brazil's Justice Ministry on Friday said it was investigating allegations that Ford's Brazilian unit set "abusive prices" for car parts and forced distributors to buy a certain number of specific vehicle models.
Ford do Brasil Ltda, Brazil's fourth-largest automaker, declined to comment on the investigation.
The ministry said in a statement that it was launching the probe on behalf of distributors, who also accuse the automaker of blocking competition among dealers.
Distributors claim Ford is requiring them to buy specific amounts of cars and car parts, the ministry said. Distributors also say Ford charges "abusive prices" for parts, it said.
In addition, dealers complain that Ford is undercutting them by selling cars directly from the factory.
The Justice Ministry will submit a report of its investigation to Brazil's antitrust commission (CADE), which will rule on the issue.
If CADE rules against Ford, the automaker will have to pay a fine and end the practices, the Justice Ministry said.
Ford sold 131,818 vehicles in Brazil in the first nine months of the year.
